Rusting of iron is electrochemical in nature

Rusting of iron is an electrochemical phenomenon in which one spot of iron acts as anode.

$Fe\left(s\right) \to Fe^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + 2e^{-}$

These electrons move through the metal and are taken up by the oxygen already dissolved in water in presence of $H^{+}$ furnished by ${H}_{2}C{O}_{3}$ , which is formed by the dissolution of $C{O}_{2} \left(g\right)$ in water. Since increase in the concentration of $H^{+}$ results in the increase in the rate of the reaction, therefore, rusting of iron occurs quicker, when the concentration of dissolved $C{O}_{2}$ in water increases.

$Fe^{2 +}$ so-obtained are further oxidized to $F{e}_{2}{O}_{3}$ by atmospheric oxygen. $F{e}_{2}{O}_{3}$ is then hydrated to form rust.

$F{e}_{2}{O}_{3} + x{H}_{2}O \to \mathop{F{e}_{2}{O}_{3}. x{H}_{2}O}_{\left(Rust\right)}$

questions.q:
Select the set having incorrect statements given here.
(i) Manganese exhibits +7 oxidation state
(ii) Zinc forms coloured ions
(iii) $[ \text{Co}{\text{F}_{6}{]}^{3 -}$ is diamagnetic
(iv) Sc forms +4 oxidation state
(v) Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state

Outer electronic configuration of Mn is $\text{3}{\textd^{5}\text{4}{\texts^{2}$ which means it can show +7 oxidation state also (correct)
Zinc does not form coloured ions as it has completely filled $\text{3}{\textd^{10}\text{4}{\texts^{2}$ configuration.
In $[ \text{Co}{\text{F}_{6}{]}^{3 -}, \text{C}{\texto^{3 +}$ is a $d^{6}$ system. Fluoride is a weak field ligand and hence it can not cause pairing of electrons.

Sc can show a maximum of +3 oxidation state as it has an outer electronic configuration of $\text{3}{\textd^{1}\text{4}{\texts^{2}$.
Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state as this oxidation state is the most stable one for it.
Hence (ii), (iii), (iv) are incorrect while (i), (v) are correct.
